facts.statement: The type species A. meyeri was named in 1871 based on a single specimen found in Cerin, eastern France.
facts.quote: The type species is A. meyeri, named in 1871 from a single specimen from Cerin, eastern France.

facts.statement: Two nominal species, A. franconicum (named in 1906) and A. paintenense (named in 1961), were based on missing specimens from Bavaria and later synonymized, with A. franconicum having priority.
facts.quote: Two more nominal species, A. franconicum, named in 1906, and A paintenense, named in 1961, are based on now-missing specimens from Bavaria, southern Germany, and were synonymized into a single species, for which A. franconicum has priority.

facts.statement: A 2016 review removed A. franconicum from the genus Alligatorium and placed it in Neosuchia incertae sedis.
facts.quote: A 2016 review of Atoposauridae removed A. franconicum from Alligatorium and placed at Neosuchia incertae sedis.

facts.statement: The species A. depereti, described in 1915, was reassigned to the separate genus Montsecosuchus in 1988.
facts.quote: Alligatorium depereti, described in 1915, was reassigned to its own genus, Montsecosuchus, in 1988.

facts.statement: Alligatorium belongs to the parent group Atoposauridae.
Alligatorium is classified in the family Atoposauridae.
Alligatorium is classified in the class Reptilia.
Alligatorium lived during the Kimmeridgian stage, between 154.8 and 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (154.8 to 149.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Alligatorium is an extinct genus of atoposaurid crocodylomorph found in Late Jurassic marine deposits in France.
rejected.quote: Alligatorium is an extinct genus of atoposaurid crocodylomorph from Late Jurassic marine deposits in France.
